summary.text: James Comer is the Republican incumbent for Kentucky's 1st Congressional District, in office since November 2016. A Monroe County farmer and agribusiness owner, he served in the Kentucky House of Representatives and as Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture before Congress. He chairs the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and also sits on the Education and Workforce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Comer was born in Carthage, Tennessee, in 1972 and, according to his official biography, was raised in Monroe County, Kentucky.
He earned a bachelor's degree in agriculture from Western Kentucky University in 1993 and started his first farm.

His business career includes co-owning the Comer Land and Cattle Company since 1994, serving as president of Comer and Polston Insurance Incorporated from 1993 to 1995 and of CFB Foods Incorporated from 2001 to 2003, and serving as a director of South Central Bank from 2000 to 2012.
Comer chaired the Monroe County Republican Party and served in the Kentucky House of Representatives, District 53, from 2001 to 2012, a span of six terms.
He was elected Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture in 2011 and held the office from 2012 to 2016; his official biography says he championed Kentucky's industrial hemp industry in that role.
Comer sought the 2015 Republican nomination for governor and lost the May 19 primary to Matt Bevin by 83 votes.
He took office in the U.S. House on November 14, 2016, succeeding Ed Whitfield, and was renominated in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary.
In Congress he chairs the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and also serves on the Education and Workforce Committee.
